title: Investigate shared KV slab pointer rotation causing cross-worker aliasing and numerical drift
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We are observing sporadic numerical drift (softmax output skew and token misalignment) in long-context prefill->decode runs on multi-GPU Dedicated nodes. Initial investigation points to the shared KV slab allocator: during slab reclamation and shard migration we see a pointer rotation race where two workers temporarily alias the same slab memory region. This produces stale KV entries being read by a different stream which leads to subtle softmax perturbation and rare token shifts in generated outputs.

Why this matters:
- Correctness: downstream decoding can diverge leading to nondeterministic outputs for the same request observed across retries.
- Reliability: causes hard-to-reproduce production regressions on long-horizon chat sessions and batched requests.
- Performance: current mitigation (global allocator lock) significantly regresses throughput for high-concurrency workloads.

Observed symptoms / telemetry:
- Increased softmax variance on sequences > 1024 tokens (90th percentile) correlated with KV eviction events.
- Error-rate spike on a handful of customer workloads during overnight batches; not an outright crash.
- Sampling of process memory maps shows same slab address referenced by two different worker threads for ~5-20ms windows.
- Trace shows slab migrate path called concurrently from Prefill finalize and Background shard compactor.

Reproduction steps (non-deterministic):
1) Start dedicated runtime on 8xA100 nodes with concurrent prefill streams (batch size 16) and high frequency of short-lived inference jobs.
2) Prime KV store with multiple long-context conversations (sequence length ~2048).
3) Trigger artifact: run the 'long-horizon stress' harness for 30 minutes.
4) Collect traces and heap/slab maps when softmax variance threshold exceeded.

Initial triage findings:
- Root cause hypothesis: slab allocator uses a per-shard freelist but relies on a migration handshake that is non-atomic across worker A (evict) and worker B (adopt). A reorder in the migration steps allows B to see a pointer to a slab before the ownership bit and epoch are updated, causing transient aliasing.
- Kernel path: aliasing leads to KV reads returning old values for specific kv (layer idx, head idx) resulting in small but compounding numerical differences in attention scores.
- Race window measured at 2-30ms depending on compaction frequency and CPU scheduling.

Short-term mitigations tried:
- Global allocator lock during migration: fixes correctness but reduces throughput ~18% under heavy load.
- Increase epoch fencing: reduces incidence but does not eliminate race under high concurrency.
- Rate-limit compactor: drops occurrence but unacceptable for long runs (memory bleed).

Proposed fix plan (3 phased):
Phase A (safety): Add an atomic migrate flag and two-phase publish (mark->copy->publish) to guarantee consumers never read partially-published slab pointers. Keep as a short-term feature flag to enable rollforward without full rollout. Estimate 3 points.
Phase B (perf): Implement per-shard versioned pointer with lock-free double-buffering for slab handoff. This avoids global locks while preserving atomicity. New handoff uses atomic compare-and-swap on pointer+version pair. Estimate 5 points.
Phase C (validation + rollout): Add deterministic stress harness, fuzzing for allocator races, concrete unit tests that simulate scheduler preemption and compactor interleaving. Gradual canary on dedicated pool and telemetry SLOs. Estimate 2 points.

Telemetry / instrumentation changes required:
- Emit allocator events: MIGRATE_START, MIGRATE_COPY_DONE, MIGRATE_PUBLISH with shard id, slab addr, epoch, worker id.
- Add sampling for slab alias windows to correlate with softmax variance.
- Dashboard: per-node allocator race rate and average alias window duration.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for two-phase publish semantics and CAS retries.
- Deterministic simulation harness that replays recorded interleavings and scheduler preemptions.
- Perf benchmark comparing throughput and latency on baseline, Phase A flag, and Phase B implementation.
- Canary rollout to dedicated cluster with shadowing enabled (no external customer traffic initially).

Rollback criteria for rollout:
- Any reproducible increase in token divergence rate relative to baseline >0.1% at 95th percentile during canary.
- Throughput regressions >5% (unless explicitly accepted for first rollout and compensated elsewhere).

Related artifacts and links:
- Internal log dump: gs://redwood-logs/2025/02/kv-slab-alias-sample-20250219.log
- Repro harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/allocator-fuzz
- Prior related tickets: ENG-31822 (kv-buffer-offset-rotation), ENG-37456 (async-kernel-pruning-token-reorder).

Acceptance criteria:
- Phase B implemented with no observed slab alias windows in deterministic harness and <1e-6 observed alias rate in 72 hour production canary.
- No increase in token divergence in canary; throughput within -5% of baseline.
